correctness.rationale: The verified primary Proposition 11 proves the exact dual-incidence replacement and extremality under interior dangling insertion. For the dual arc circle of radius rho=sqrt(1-s^2/4), the two channel endpoint functions are 2rho sin(t/2) and 2asin(rho sin(t/2)). Their exact second derivatives are negative on each exposed minor arc for all s>0, so Jensen gives the unique equiangular optimizer, positive gain, and strict monotonicity with r. The two Taylor expansions have coefficients rho/24 and rho(1-rho^2)/24, implying precisely the stated r^-2 rates with r^-4 remainders. Every finite extremal configuration can be strictly improved by one midpoint insertion, so no finite maximizer exists; the primary Theorem 15 bounds the spherical product, and L<=theta bounds the Euclidean one. The packaged symbolic checker independently reconstructs the differentiation and Taylor certificates and checks the tetrahedron case.

value.rationale: The spherical dual-edge product is the exact global discrete reformulation of a central unsolved constant-width surface-area problem. The theorem proves that the global optimization cannot have a finite extremal-graph maximizer and thus clarifies the mathematical status of the supremum, independently of numerical fixed-graph experiments. The unique equiangular subdivision and sharp quadratic rate give a natural optimal mesh rule and a precise complexity benchmark for the finite dangling decorations actually used in the source. These structural results go beyond nonnegative monotonicity, require no artificial parameter slice, and make no unwarranted claim about the unknown global supremum.
